subject: Two stage latent model (not sure what else to call it)

messages.author: 32bf4f27a31a68db
messages.subject: Two stage latent model (not sure what else to call it)
parts:
Hello,

I'm trying to figure out if INLA can help me model something involving two "stages".

As an illustrative example:

We'll model the probability of a student getting accepted to university as a basic logistic regression with 4-5 covariates.

One of those covariates is their SAT score.

The SAT score is log-normally distributed and depends on 3-4 additional covariates (different than what is in the logistic model.)

In rough math:

P(Accept) ~ 1/(1+exp(-eta))
eta = cov_1 * beta_1 + cov_2 * beta_2 + SAT * beta_3
SAT ~ N(mu, sigma)
mu = cov_4 * beta_4 + cov_5 * beta_5 + cov_6 * beta_6


The idea is that for a student who doesn't have an SAT score yet, we will sample possible scores from the posterior of the log-normal model, then use those samples as input to the logistic regression, where will again sample from the posterior of the logistic regression model. In layman's terms "The uncertainty of the SAT score will carry through and influence the uncertainty of the logistic model"

Is modeling something like this possible in INLA?

Thanks!!

journal = JRSSC,
keywords = {year2015,my.own,my.cv},
year = 2015,
volume = 64,
number = 2,
pages = {231--252}
}
